source.title: Does your LLM truly unlearn? An embarrassingly simple approach to recover unlearned knowledge
source.authors: Zhi-Wei Zhang; Fali Wang; Xiao-Min Li; Zongyu Wu; Xianfeng Tang; Hui Liu; Qi He; Wen-Peng Yin; Su-Hang Wang

record.file_problem: The text is the full paper, though its title in the body is “Catastrophic Failure of LLM Unlearning via Quantization,” which differs from the supplied title.
record.tranche_reason: It tests whether an attack—quantizing unlearned weights—recovers forgotten knowledge, using its own experiments and measures.
record.gate_note: The study also reports results for metrics other than knowledge memorization, including verbatim memorization, privacy leakage and utility. Rows below focus on direct knowledge-memorization measures and the RWKU knowledge probes. Its theoretical discussion and cited results are not recorded as experimental rows.
record.test_reason: The study applies post-training quantization (RTN 8/4-bit, AWQ, GPTQ) to unlearned LLMs and measures forget-set knowledge (MUSE KnowMem; RWKU FB/QA/AA) before and after. This is a different attack on the same question: is unlearned knowledge deleted or only hidden? It also proposes and tests SURE as a quantization-robust method. It is not one of the claim's listed original sources.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that 4-bit quantization (RTN, AWQ, GPTQ) restores much 'forgotten' knowledge for utility-constrained unlearning methods: on average 21% retained in full precision vs 83% after 4-bit. They find 8-bit behaves like full precision and explain the effect by small unlearning weight changes falling within quantization bins. SURE (saliency-masked, large learning rate) mitigates recovery, but they call it highly hyperparameter-sensitive and note a utility trade-off; it does not fully solve the problem.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates quantization as a post-unlearning attack, rather than reproducing the original sources' methods. It also proposes SURE as a quantization-robust unlearning method.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery depends on quantization precision and technique, unlearning method, dataset and utility constraints. The authors report substantially greater problems at 4-bit than 8-bit; RTN, AWQ and GPTQ show similar effects in the reported NEWS experiments.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. The quantization results vary by method and dataset; the authors note that GA's apparent forgetting is confounded by severe utility loss and that SURE is sensitive to hyperparameter selection.
record.rows_left_out: The NEWS Table 1 and Table 2 results for metrics other than KnowMem on Dforget were not included because they do not directly measure recovery of targeted knowledge. BOOKS Table 1 comparisons and SURE results on NEWS (Table 8) were not extracted as rows; the paper's main tables and text describe these findings, but the selected rows prioritize direct, clearly aligned knowledge-memorization results and SURE's BOOKS quantization comparison.

untested.parts: Near-chance accuracy on multiple-choice hazard benchmarks (e.g. WMDP) and general-ability benchmarks for the original methods. Knowledge is measured by ROUGE on QA, not accuracy.
All: no relearning or fine-tuning attack is run.
All: no activation-direction ablation. Only a theoretical weight-rounding argument for hiding versus deleting.
2-bit and below (excluded), quantization-aware training, and models other than 7B (LLaMA-2 7B, ICLM-7B, RWKU model). Not tested on WMDP or Harry Potter-style original setups beyond MUSE BOOKS.
All: prompting attacks are only cited from Lynch et al. (Appendix M).
SURE is tested only against quantization, not fine-tuning, activation edits or prompting. Only RTN 4-bit is tested on SURE.

missing.what: BOOKS KnowMem on Dforget before/after 8- and 4-bit RTN for all six methods. Includes the headline GA_KLR result, 15.1 to 34.6 (8-bit 10.1), and GA_GDR 2.9 to 33.7, NPO_GDR 13.4 to 31.9, NPO_KLR 13.7 to 34.2, NPO 0 to 5.3.
AWQ/GPTQ KnowMem for GA_GDR (28.9 to 50.7/50.4), NPO_KLR (36.6 to 52.0/51.1) and NPO (0 to 25.3/25.3).
SURE on NEWS. Quantized KnowMem 34.6/34.6/35.9/29.3 vs non-SURE 4-bit 50.1/50.9/51.4/53.7. But SURE full-precision KnowMem is higher than the originals for GA methods (e.g. 38.5 vs 28.9).
SURE utility costs: GA_GDR+SURE truthfulness 0.2 and factuality 0.0. Hyperparameter sensitivity reported.
Verbatim memorization recovery, e.g. BOOKS GA_KLR M1 13.0 to 75.6 and NPO_KLR 12.4 to 70.9 at 4-bit.
Headline aggregate: utility-constrained methods retain 21% of forgotten knowledge in full precision vs 83% after 4-bit.

record.verdict_notes: The reader misaligned the NEWS Table 1 M2 column for NPO-family rows; r8-r11 are corrected above. Table 3 reports full-precision BOOKS KnowMem for GA_KLR/NPO_GDR/NPO_KLR (25.1/27.4/22.7) that differ from Table 1 (15.1/13.4/13.7) for the same methods, an internal inconsistency worth flagging. RMU/RMU_LAT baselines have zero retain utility, which weakens r17/r18 as tests of utility-preserving unlearning. Version A rows are linked here because quantization recovery directly contradicts 'simple attacks don't recover it'. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests recovery through quantization, not whether simple attacks generally fail; it does not report general-ability results for the original unlearning methods.
No recovery by fine-tuning on a small relearning set is tested.
No activation-direction ablation or access-versus-deletion analysis is tested.
The study tests post-training 4-bit and 8-bit quantization, including RTN, AWQ and GPTQ, but not every quantization method or precision.
No recovery by rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages or in-context information is tested.
SURE is evaluated against quantization recovery, not against fine-tuning, activation edits or prompting attacks.

relationships.reason: Forget-set knowledge rises from about 27 to about 50 on NEWS (target 63.9) (r4, r6, r12, r13, r14). RWKU probes rise sharply (r19-r21, r26, r27). RMU rises 0 to about 28 (r17, r18).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: 4-bit quantization of utility-constrained methods on NEWS, and the reported RWKU GA results
reader_labels.reason: Knowledge-memorization measures rise substantially after quantization in these settings (r4, r6, r10, r12, r19-r21).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: 8-bit quantization, NPO on RWKU, and RT on RWKU
reader_labels.reason: Recovery is absent or smaller for some 8-bit and NPO cases, while RT's FB score improves after quantization; the paper attributes that exception to utility loss (r1, r3, r5, r7, r9, r11, r22-r27).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GA_GDR + SURE on BOOKS, after 4-bit quantization
reader_labels.reason: SURE substantially reduces Dforget KnowMem relative to the same method quantized without SURE (r28).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: GA_KLR + SURE and NPO_GDR + SURE on BOOKS, after 4-bit quantization
reader_labels.reason: SURE improves on the corresponding quantized comparison but does not eliminate measurable knowledge memorization (r29-r30).
